scenes.narration: An audit function, separate from compliance, that tests the AML/CTF programme on a risk basis and reports to the board.

scenes.heading: Trained, tested people
scenes.narration: Training for everyone before they start and repeatedly after, deeper training for due diligence staff, specialist training for compliance and audit, and annual knowledge tests.

scenes.heading: Evidence
scenes.narration: Records kept for at least ten years, and files that let SAMA reconstruct transactions, decisions and training.

scenes.heading: Consequences
scenes.narration: Where controls fail, SAMA can warn, order corrections, fine up to SAR 5 million per violation, remove managers or restrict and revoke licences.

cards.title: Stages of a business risk assessment (Dec 2025 guidance)
cards.caption: Profitability must not influence risk ratings, and a group member must assess its own risks rather than rely only on the group assessment.

items.label: 1. Collect data
items.detail: National risk assessment, committee findings, SAMA instructions, internal customer and transaction data.

items.label: 2. Analyse inherent risk
items.detail: Structural, customer, product, channel, geographic, technology and emerging risks.

items.label: 3. Assess mitigation
items.detail: Test the controls: automated or manual, preventive or detective, independently tested?

items.label: 4. Respond to residual risk
items.detail: Compare with risk appetite and build an action plan for gaps.

items.label: 5. Endorse
items.detail: Document, approve and share results with staff through continuous training.

items.label: 6. Follow up and review
items.detail: Update on trigger events and at least annually; notify SAMA of new risks.

cards.question: What is the difference between inherent and residual risk in SAMA's December 2025 business risk guidance?
options: Inherent risk is before mitigation measures; residual risk is what remains after them
Inherent risk applies to customers; residual risk applies to products
Inherent risk is set by SAMA; residual risk is set by the bank
They mean the same thing in the Saudi guidance
cards.explanation: The guidance defines inherent risk as the level before preventive and mitigation measures and residual risk as what remains after they are effectively applied. Residual risk is then compared with the bank's risk appetite.

cards.title: Who is responsible for what?
cards.prompt: Match each function to its duty in SAMA's AML/CTF Guide.

pairs.right: Provides sufficient resources and receives regular reports on AML/CTF and risk assessment
Senior-level officer who works independently and reports to the board and its committees
Specialised team, solely Saudi nationals, with the competence to run the programme
Tests the programme on a risk basis, separate from the functions it audits
Approves policies and high-risk classifications and fixes audit findings

cards.title: SAMA's training rules in one place
cards.body:
Section 11 of SAMA's AML/CTF Guide builds on Article 14/1(e) of the AML regulation and Article 18 of the CTF regulations:

- **Budget:** allocate enough budget to train senior management and staff.
- **Content:** inspired by real experiences, covering new ML/TF methods and the bank's own controls.
- **Everyone (11.2):** from board members, committees and executives to all staff, matched to role and level.
- **Before starting work:** new joiners are trained before they start, and training is repeated.
- **Deeper for some:** fuller training for staff doing due diligence; specialised training for compliance and internal audit.
- **Penalties awareness:** all staff and directors learn their duties and the penalties for failure.
- **External trainers (11.3):** check suitability, trainer background and trainee feedback.
- **Testing (11.4):** assess knowledge and training quality at least annually.
- **Records (11.5):** documents, attendance and dates of training.

cards.title: Which training rule is this?
cards.prompt: Sort each requirement by the SAMA text that sets it.

items.text: Test staff knowledge at least once a year
Train new employees before they start work
Check an external trainer's academic and work history
Run simulation exercises for sanctions specialists
Hold in-person workshops for the TFS unit
Give the board focused awareness on sanctions responsibilities
Do not assign a teller before KYC, AML/CFT and ethics courses
Include extensive training on the account opening rules

lines.text: What actually happens to an institution that gets this wrong? Give me real examples, not theory.

SAMA publishes its decisions on exchange companies. In 2019 it cancelled the licence of an exchange company after inspections, follow-up visits and meetings with its management, because it could not fix its AML/CFT deficiencies.
A whole licence?
Yes. And since 2017 SAMA has required banks to publish SAMA's punitive decisions in their annual reports, with a category for AML/CTF due diligence violations. Shareholders see it.
So the cost is not only the fine. It is the disclosure, the remediation and the trust.
Then we fix the training records this week, not next month.

cards.title: Real cases: SAMA acts on AML/CFT failures (2019)
cards.body:
SAMA's own announcements show how supervisory action escalates:

- **March 2019, Mohamed Mounir Halawani Sons Exchange Company:** SAMA cancelled the company's exchange licence. Its fund transfer activity had been suspended in September 2017. SAMA said it had carried out inspection visits on AML/CFT compliance, follow-up visits on the corrective action plan and meetings with senior management, and in the end found the company unable to fix all the deficiencies. The decision relied on SAMA's powers under the AML Law, the terrorism financing law and the money changing rules.
- **2019, Saeed Mohammed Ali Al-Amoudi & Co:** SAMA revoked the company's licence to transfer funds inside and outside the Kingdom, citing violations of the AML Law, the CTF Law, their regulations and the AML/CTF rules, while allowing its other licensed activities to continue.

**For a bank:** corrective action plans are tested, deadlines matter, and SAMA can remove specific activities as well as whole licences.

cards.title: The missing training records
cards.situation: Two days before SAMA's visit, Faisal confirms that two new tellers attended the AML/CFT course before starting, but the learning system lost their completion records. One teller also missed this year's knowledge test while on leave. A colleague suggests backdating the records and marking the test as passed 'since they clearly know the material'.

choices.text: Backdate the records and mark the test as passed to avoid a finding
choices.outcome: Falsifying records is a serious integrity breach and would make any finding far worse. SAMA expects honest, auditable training records.

choices.text: Rebuild the records from genuine evidence such as attendance sheets and trainer confirmations, record the gap and its cause, schedule the missed test now and tell SAMA's team openly if asked
choices.outcome: Best choice. It restores real evidence for Guide 11.5, meets the annual testing expectation in 11.4 and shows a control that finds and fixes its own gaps.

choices.text: Say nothing and hope the sample SAMA chooses does not include those tellers
choices.outcome: Hoping for luck leaves a known gap unfixed and undermines trust if it is discovered.

choices.text: Remove the two tellers from the counter until they repeat the course
choices.outcome: This is cautious but unnecessary if genuine evidence shows they attended. Fixing the record and the missed test is the right remedy.

cards.title: Supervisory measures and criminal penalties
cards.caption: Figures are from the 2017 AML Law as published in the SAMA Rulebook. Amendments to the law were reported in 2026: always check the current official text.

items.label: Money
items.left: Fine up to SAR 5m per violation

items.label: Other measures
items.left: Warnings, orders, bans, removal, licence action

items.label: Legal persons
items.right: Fine up to SAR 50m, at least double the funds

cards.back: The first of nine supervisory measures in Article 25; others include orders to comply and regular progress reports.
SAMA can ban individuals from working in the sectors it supervises, for a period it sets.
SAMA can restrict the powers of, dismiss or replace directors and executives, or appoint temporary controllers.
A travel ban for a period equal to the prison term served for money laundering (Art. 28).
Deportation, with no possibility of return to the Kingdom (Art. 28).
Fine of SAR 3m to SAR 10m where a TF crime is committed in its name (Art. 49).

cards.question: Which statement about SAMA's AML/CTF compliance function is correct under Section 9 of its Guide?
options: The officer reports to the head of retail banking
The officer is at senior management level and reports to the board and its committees
The function may be fully outsourced to the external auditor
The function only needs staff during SAMA inspections
cards.explanation: Guide 9.1 requires a senior-level officer working independently and reporting administratively and technically to the board and its committees, with timely access to all needed information.

items.label: AML Law and CTF Law
items.detail: Royal Decrees M/20 and M/21 replace the earlier laws.

items.label: Penalty publication
items.detail: Banks must publish SAMA punitive decisions in annual reports.

items.label: CTF regulations, Guide, rules
items.detail: CTF implementing regulations, Account Opening Rules and the AML/CTF Guide.

items.label: Licence cancelled
items.detail: SAMA cancels an exchange company licence over AML/CFT deficiencies.

items.label: TFS Rules
items.detail: New Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions.

items.label: Business risk guidance
items.detail: ML, TF and PF business risk assessment guidance.

cards.title: Your exam checklist
cards.body:
Before the final boss, make sure you can:

- Name the laws, regulations and SAMA texts and what each adds.
- List the CDD triggers, the 25% test and the PEP measures.
- Describe the reporting route, the technical report and the tipping-off ban.
- Recite the screening moments, alert handling and freeze rules.
- Explain the business risk assessment stages, the compliance and audit roles, the training rules, ten-year records and the penalties.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: The December 2025 guidance requires a bank-specific business risk assessment that separates ML, TF and PF risk, is audited independently and is updated at least annually.
The AML/CTF officer is senior and independent and reports to the board; the AML/CTF unit is specialised and adequately resourced; audit tests it independently.
Training: everyone, before starting and repeatedly; deeper for CDD staff; specialist for compliance and audit; tested at least annually; recorded.
SAMA can warn, order, fine up to SAR 5 million per violation, ban or remove people and restrict or revoke licences; courts impose prison and large fines for the crimes.
SAMA's own announcements show escalation from warnings and corrective plans to suspension and licence cancellation.

cards.prompt: If a SAMA inspector sat with your team tomorrow, which record or decision would you be least comfortable explaining? What would make it easier to defend?

quiz.question: How often must the business risk assessment be updated under SAMA's December 2025 guidance, if no trigger event occurs first?
options: At least once every three years
At least once a year
Only when SAMA requests it
At least once every five years
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 2.11(g) of the guidance requires ongoing updates at least annually, and paragraph 2.5 requires an immediate update when new or increasing risk elements appear.

quiz.question: Wahat Bank belongs to a regional group that already has a group-wide business risk assessment. What does SAMA's guidance (2.8) require?
options: The group assessment is enough on its own
SAMA prepares the assessment for group members
Only the parent bank's board must approve it
Wahat Bank must also assess its own risks individually
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 2.8 says a financial institution in a group must carry out its own individual assessment and not rely solely on the group assessment.

quiz.question: Which of these is NOT allowed to influence a customer or business risk rating under SAMA's December 2025 guidance (3.2.4)?
options: The profitability of the relationship
The customer's transaction patterns
The delivery channel used
The country the customer trades with
quiz.explanation: The guidance says economic or profitability considerations must not influence the risk classification. Country, channel and transaction patterns are legitimate risk factors.

quiz.question: To whom does the AML/CTF compliance officer report under SAMA Guide 9.1?
options: The Saudi FIU
The external auditor
The board of directors and its committees
The head of the largest business line
quiz.explanation: Guide 9.1 requires the officer to work independently and report administratively and technically to the board and its committees.

quiz.question: What is the maximum fine SAMA may impose as a supervisory measure under Article 25 of the AML Law, as published in the SAMA Rulebook?
options: SAR 5 million per violation
SAR 1 million per year
SAR 500,000 per violation
SAR 50 million per violation
quiz.explanation: Article 25 allows a fine of up to SAR 5 million per violation, alongside warnings, orders, bans, removal of managers and licence measures. SAR 50 million is the criminal ceiling for legal persons in Article 31.

quiz.question: Which staff does SAMA Guide 11.2(c) single out for specialised and adequate AML/CTF training?
options: Only IT staff who run monitoring systems
Only staff based at head office
Compliance function staff and independent audit staff
Only branch managers and tellers
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.2(c) requires specialised training for the AML/CTF compliance function and the independent audit function; 11.2(b) adds fuller training for staff doing due diligence.

quiz.question: Wahat Bank hires an external institute to deliver AML training. What does SAMA Guide 11.3 expect?
options: Accept any institute with an international licence
Use only institutes that SAMA owns
Let the institute set and approve the bank's AML policy
Check the training's fit and the trainer's background, and survey trainees
quiz.explanation: Guide 11.3 asks the bank to verify the training suits AML/CTF requirements and its risks, check the trainer's academic and work history, and poll trainees on the materials and trainer.

quiz.question: Under SAMA's 2017 instructions on publishing banking penalties, where must a bank disclose SAMA's punitive decisions?
options: Only in a confidential letter to SAMA
In its annual report, by type of violation, number and total fines
Nowhere, as SAMA decisions are confidential
On a notice board in each branch
quiz.explanation: The instructions require banks to publish SAMA punitive decisions in their annual reports, with the type of violation (including AML/CTF due diligence), the number of decisions and the total fines, and SAMA republishes them.

quiz.question: What did SAMA cite when it cancelled Mohamed Mounir Halawani Sons Exchange Company's licence in March 2019?
options: The partners asked SAMA to cancel the licence
It could not fix all identified AML/CFT deficiencies after inspections and follow-up
The company had merged with a bank
The company failed a capital adequacy test
quiz.explanation: SAMA's announcement said inspection and follow-up visits and meetings with management took place, and SAMA found the company unable to address all AML/CFT deficiencies. A partner-requested cancellation was a different 2019 case.

quiz.question: A non-Saudi convicted of money laundering finishes his prison term. What does Article 28 of the AML Law provide?
options: A fine equal to the laundered amount
A travel ban equal to the prison term
Supervision by SAMA for five years
Deportation with no possibility of returning to the Kingdom
quiz.explanation: Article 28 provides for deportation of non-Saudis after the penalty, with no return. The travel ban equal to the prison term applies to Saudi nationals.

regulators: General Directorate of Financial Intelligence (Saudi FIU, SAFIU)

references.title: Implementing Regulation to the Anti-Money Laundering Law
references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Risk assessment, due diligence triggers and content, beneficial ownership, PEPs, internal controls including ongoing employee training, report content, good-faith protection and FIU powers.

references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Money laundering offence, preventive duties, record keeping for ten years, reporting to the FIU, tipping-off ban, supervisory measures and criminal penalties.

references.title: Law on Combating Terrorism Crimes and its Financing (Royal Decree No. M/21, as amended)
references.issuer: Government of Saudi Arabia (SAMA Rulebook copy)
references.note: Terrorist financing offence covering funds from any source, preventive duties, reporting to the FIU, tipping-off ban, failure to report and supervisory measures.

references.title: Implementing Regulations of the Law of Combating Terrorist Crimes and its Financing
references.note: CFT policies and procedures must include continuing employee training programmes, staff screening and an independent audit procedure.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Training for all staff and for new staff before they start, repeated over time; deeper training for due diligence staff; specialised training for compliance and audit; board included; knowledge testing at least annually; training records kept.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Documented risk assessment approved by senior management, customer risk classification with senior approval for high risk, and assessment of new products before launch.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Customer acceptance policy, due diligence triggers and minimum content, independent verification sources, ongoing due diligence and sanctions list checks.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Tools to identify PEPs, foreign PEPs always high risk, same measures for family and close associates, and documented grounds for rating a local PEP below high risk.

references.title: The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Guide
references.note: Board-approved reporting procedures, prompt reports to the FIU including attempts, technical report with six months of statements, documented decisions not to report, and staff awareness.

references.title: Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions
references.note: Governance, screening moments, list management, maker-checker alert handling, freezing without delay and without prior notice, notifying SAMA, lifting freezes, ten-year records and role-based training with simulations.

references.title: Guidance on Assessing Business Risks Related to Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, and Proliferation Financing
references.note: Bank-specific business risk assessment separating ML, TF and PF risk, six stages from data collection to review, annual update and independent audit, and staff awareness of results.

references.title: Account Opening Rules
references.provision: Chapter II, Rule 9 (Training as a Key Principle for these Rules)
references.note: Banks may not assign teller or customer service staff until they have attended courses on KYC, AML/CFT and banker ethics, and must run continuing on-the-job training covering these rules.

bank.question: A compliance trainee says the SAMA AML/CTF Guide is 'the law' on money laundering. Which correction is most accurate?
options: The Guide applies only to exchange companies, not banks
The Guide is optional advice with no supervisory weight
The Guide replaced the AML Law in 2019, so the trainee is right
The offences and core duties are in the AML Law; the Guide sets SAMA's expectations for meeting them
bank.explanation: The 2017 AML Law and its implementing regulation create the offences and duties; SAMA's 2019 Guide, issued as a circular, explains how SAMA expects institutions it supervises to comply. It does not replace the law and is not optional.

bank.question: A customer converts proceeds of a fraud into gold to hide their origin. The fraudster has not yet been tried. Can the bank's suspicion and a money laundering case proceed?
options: Only if the fraud happened inside the Kingdom
Yes: money laundering is a separate offence needing no prior predicate conviction
Only if the gold is worth over SAR 1 million
No: the fraud must be proven in court first
bank.explanation: Article 4 of the AML Law makes money laundering independent of a predicate conviction, wherever the predicate crime occurred, and the reporting duty applies whatever the amount.

bank.question: Which combination correctly describes the Saudi FIU?
options: It receives and analyses reports, has operational independence and is overseen by the President of State Security
It is part of the Public Prosecution and prosecutes ML cases
It is a committee of bank compliance officers chaired by SAMA
It is a SAMA department that also inspects banks and imposes fines
bank.explanation: Article 17 establishes the General Directorate of Financial Intelligence as the national centre for receiving and analysing reports, operationally independent and overseen by the President of State Security. Inspection and fines are SAMA's role; prosecution belongs to the Public Prosecution.

bank.question: A relative of a customer collects cash from a mosque congregation and sends it abroad to an entity tied to a terrorist group. He says the donors earned the money honestly. How does Article 47 of the CTF Law treat the honest origin?
options: It reduces the offence to an administrative breach
It matters only if the donors knew the purpose
It is irrelevant; funds from legitimate sources are covered
It is a full defence to terrorist financing
bank.explanation: Article 47 expressly covers funds from legitimate or illegitimate sources provided or collected with the intention or knowledge that they will be used for terrorism or by a terrorist entity.

bank.question: A board member of Wahat Bank argues that, because the bank as a legal person is liable for money laundering in its name, directors cannot be prosecuted personally. What does the AML Law say?
options: Directors are liable only for supervisory measures, not crimes
Directors are immune while the bank remains licensed
Corporate liability does not exclude directors' and employees' personal liability
Only the chairman can be held personally liable
bank.explanation: Article 3 states that a legal person's criminal liability does not exclude that of chairmen, board members, owners, employees and others who acted in its name or for its account.

bank.question: Which SAMA text requires training on AML/CTF to draw on real experiences and include new ML/TF methods, with a sufficient budget?
options: Chapter Six of the TFS Rules
Section 6 of SAMA's AML/CTF Guide
Article 25 of the AML Law
Section 11 of SAMA's AML/CTF Guide
bank.explanation: The introduction to Section 11 asks institutions to budget for training and to base it on real experiences, new ML/TF methods and internal controls. Section 6 deals with record keeping and Chapter Six of the TFS Rules with freezing.

bank.question: A new hire at Wahat Bank's call centre will answer customer queries about accounts from next week. Which approach best matches SAMA's expectations?
options: Complete AML/CTF training before she starts, then refresh and test it at least annually
Let her start now and train her within her first year
Train her only if she later moves to a branch
Give her the policy to read and skip formal training
bank.explanation: Guide 11.2(a) requires training for new staff before they start work, repeated over time, and 11.4 requires knowledge testing at least annually. Customer service roles are also covered by Account Opening Rule 9.

bank.question: SAMA suspended an exchange company in 2017 for not complying with regulatory requirements, including AML/CTF measures. According to SAMA's statement, what had happened before the suspension?
options: The FIU had frozen all its accounts
SAMA had already issued several warnings asking it to rectify its status
The company had been convicted of money laundering
The company's partners had asked for the suspension
bank.explanation: SAMA's November 2017 statement on Saleh Hussain Al-Amoudi Sons said several warnings had been issued before the suspension, which would remain until full compliance was proven.

bank.question: An act of bribery took place in another country where bribery is a crime. The bribe is later moved through a Saudi bank. Which condition must also hold for it to be a predicate offence under the AML Law?
options: The act would also be an offence under Saudi law had it occurred in the Kingdom
The bribe must exceed a threshold set by SAMA
The foreign country must have requested assistance
A Saudi national must have paid the bribe
bank.explanation: Article 1(4) includes acts abroad that are crimes where committed and would have been offences in the Kingdom. No foreign request, nationality link or threshold is needed.

bank.question: A long-standing customer, a teacher, suddenly receives large transfers from a trading company and sends them on the same day. Her CDD file is two years old. Under SAMA Guide 3.2, why must Wahat Bank apply due diligence now?
options: The trading company is a new customer of another bank
Her transactions are inconsistent with her known behaviour and information
Teachers are a high-risk occupation
Her CDD file is older than one year
bank.explanation: Guide 3.2 adds a trigger when a customer's transaction does not fit their behaviour or information, alongside suspicion and doubts about earlier data. File age alone is handled by risk-based review cycles.

bank.question: A corporate applicant has four shareholders with 24% each and a fifth with 4%. Nobody reaches 25%. What should Wahat Bank do next under Regulation 7/2(c) and Guide 3.18?
options: Accept the applicant's letter naming a beneficial owner
Treat the largest shareholder company as the owner
Record that the company has no beneficial owner
Identify who controls the company by other means, then the senior managing official if needed
bank.explanation: Where no natural person reaches 25%, the bank identifies the natural persons exercising control by other means and, as a last resort, the senior managing official, while not relying primarily on the customer's statement.

bank.question: A Saudi customer is a serving deputy governor of a provincial authority. The bank's assessment finds low corruption risk, a short, transparent career and salary-based wealth. What do SAMA's rules allow?
options: He may be rated low risk without recording reasons
He must always be rated high risk, like foreign PEPs
Rating him below high risk, with sufficient documented grounds
He is not a PEP because the role is domestic
bank.explanation: Foreign PEPs are always high risk (Guide 4.13), but local PEPs are assessed using factors in 4.15; a decision that a local PEP is not high risk needs sufficient, reasonable and documented grounds (4.16).

bank.question: Wahat Bank learns that another bank refused an applicant because of suspected money laundering. What does SAMA Guide 4.5 expect?
options: Open the account and inform the other bank
Apply EDD, find out the reasons and take additional measures
Automatically refuse the applicant
Ignore it, as other banks' decisions are confidential
bank.explanation: Guide 4.5 requires enhanced due diligence when another institution has refused a customer, an effort to understand why, and additional measures where the reason was ML/TF suspicion.

bank.question: Which measure is NOT among the enhanced due diligence examples listed in SAMA Guide 4.2?
options: Verifying the customer's job, activity or profession
Establishing source of funds at the start and for transactions
Conducting on-site visits to verify the business
Requiring the customer to keep a minimum balance
bank.explanation: Guide 4.2 lists verifying occupation, identifying source of funds or income, obtaining information on assets and transactions, on-site visits and additional documents. A minimum balance is a commercial term, not an EDD measure.

bank.question: Wahat Bank wants to let a low-risk customer use the account before identity verification is complete, to avoid disrupting payroll. What conditions do Regulation 7/3 and Guide 5.5 attach?
options: Low risk, genuine need, verification as soon as practicable and controls on use meanwhile
Written permission from SAMA in each case
None, as long as the customer signs a declaration
A guarantee from the customer's employer
bank.explanation: Delayed verification is allowed only where risk is low, delay is essential to avoid interrupting normal business, verification follows as soon as practicable and risk management measures cover use of the relationship before verification.

bank.question: A customer's brother-in-law and a business partner who co-owns a company with a foreign PEP both want accounts. How should Wahat Bank treat them?
options: Only the business partner needs enhanced measures
As ordinary customers, because neither holds public office
As a family member and a close associate, applying the same enhanced measures
Only the brother-in-law needs enhanced measures
bank.explanation: Regulation 8/3 covers relatives by blood or marriage up to the second degree; 8/4 covers people with joint beneficial ownership or close business relationships. Guide 4.14 applies the same EDD to family members and close associates.

bank.question: Wahat Bank's risk assessment is approved and filed. A year later it launches a new remote onboarding channel without reassessing risk. Which requirement has it breached?
options: Assessing ML/TF risks of new delivery mechanisms before launch
Obtaining FIU approval for new channels
Publishing the risk assessment on its website
Updating the risk assessment every ten years
bank.explanation: Regulation 5/6 and Guide 1.7 require the risks of new products, practices, delivery mechanisms and technologies to be assessed before launch or first use.

bank.question: A customer refuses to provide the information needed to complete CDD for an existing account after several requests. What do Regulation 7/8 and Guide 3.11 require?
options: Keep the account but block new products
Freeze the account until he cooperates
Ask SAMA to collect the information
End the relationship and consider reporting to the FIU
bank.explanation: If CDD cannot be completed for an existing customer, the bank must terminate the relationship and consider a suspicious transaction report. Freezing is a sanctions or court measure, not the CDD remedy.

bank.question: An internal report reaches the reporting officer. She thinks the activity is odd but has no information linking it to crime and no reasonable grounds. What does SAMA Guide 8.6 say?
options: Ask the customer for an explanation first
Report anyway, since the FIU prefers more reports
Do not report on speculation; document the review and the reasons for closing it
Escalate to SAMA instead of the FIU
bank.explanation: Guide 8.6 says reports should not rest on speculation or lack of reasonable grounds, and 8.10-8.11 require the decision not to report and its reasons to be documented and kept.

bank.question: A teller tells the AML/CTF unit about a customer's odd cash deposits, then mentions to a friend at another bank that 'compliance is looking at' that customer. Which rule did the teller breach?
options: The risk assessment duty in Article 5
The tipping-off ban in Article 16 of the AML Law
The record-keeping rule in Article 12
The wire transfer rule in Article 10
bank.explanation: Article 16 forbids employees from disclosing to the customer or any other person that a report will be, is being or has been made. The exceptions cover communications within the bank and with lawyers or competent authorities, not friends at other banks.

bank.question: The FIU stops a suspicious transfer at Wahat Bank for 72 hours. Investigators need longer. Which authority can order a provisional seizure, and for how long before a court extension is needed?
options: The Public Prosecution, for up to 60 days
The FIU, for up to 90 days
The bank's board, for up to 12 months
SAMA, for up to 30 days
bank.explanation: Regulation 17/1(q) limits the FIU's stop to 72 hours. Article 44 lets the Public Prosecution order provisional seizure for up to 60 days without prior notice, extendable by court order.

bank.question: Which of these is part of the minimum content of a suspicious transaction report under Regulation 15/4?
options: SAMA's approval of the report
The reasons for suspicion on which the employee based the report
The customer's written agreement to the report
An estimate of the predicate crime's penalty
bank.explanation: Regulation 15/4 requires names, addresses and phone numbers, a description of the transaction and parties, the amount and accounts, and the reasons for suspicion. Customer agreement would amount to tipping off.

bank.question: Wahat Bank filed a report on a customer last month. The FIU now asks the bank directly for six more months of statements on that customer. How should the bank respond?
options: Refuse until SAMA forwards the request
Provide it only after the next board meeting
Provide the information promptly and fully, as the request relates to its own report
Ask the customer for consent first
bank.explanation: Article 15(2) and Regulation 18/1 require prompt and full answers, and the FIU may ask directly when the request concerns a report the bank filed. Asking the customer would breach the tipping-off ban.

bank.question: A customer closed her account eight years ago. The Public Prosecution now asks for her CDD file. What do the rules say about retention?
options: Records are kept only while the account is open
The file may already be destroyed after five years
Only transaction records must be kept, not CDD files
The file should still exist: CDD records are kept at least ten years after the relationship ends
bank.explanation: Article 12(2) requires CDD records, account files and correspondence to be kept for at least ten years after the relationship ends, and records must be readily available to competent authorities.

bank.question: Wahat Bank's monitoring system has not been tested since installation three years ago. Which SAMA expectation does this miss?
options: Replacing the system every three years
Obtaining FIU certification of the system
Testing monitoring tools periodically, at least once a year, and documenting results
Running all monitoring manually as a back-up
bank.explanation: Guide 7.6 requires periodic testing of monitoring tools, at least annually, with documented results used to improve them. SAMA does not require replacement or FIU certification.

bank.question: A suspected launderer's lawyer asks a branch manager whether a report has been filed about his client. What is the correct response?
options: Deny it to avoid alarming the client
Confirm it, since lawyers are an allowed exception
Confirm it if the lawyer shows a power of attorney
Decline to confirm or deny, and inform the AML/CTF unit of the request
bank.explanation: The Article 16 exception covers communications with the bank's own lawyers, not disclosure to the customer's lawyer, who acts for the customer. Lying is not needed; the manager simply cannot discuss it.

bank.question: A UN listing is published at 9 pm. Wahat Bank's internal list updates the next afternoon because the vendor feed runs once a day. Which TFS Rule does this most directly breach?
options: Running comprehensive screening quarterly
Updating internal lists immediately and monitoring official sources daily
Testing screening tools annually
Keeping records for ten years
bank.explanation: Rule 4.1 requires internal lists to be updated immediately on a listing and monitored daily through official channels, with records of receipt and application times; reliance on tools does not guarantee compliance (4.2).

bank.question: After a new UN listing, Wahat Bank screens its current customers but not past transactions. What else does TFS Rule 3.4 require?
options: Review transactions from the previous twelve months for dealings with the listed person
Ask SAMA to run the historic check
Notify every customer that the list has changed
Close all accounts in the listed person's country
bank.explanation: Rule 3.4 requires a documented, auditable review of transactions in the previous twelve months, or longer where risk and resources allow, to find past dealings with newly listed persons.

bank.question: A screening alert matches a customer's name but the dates of birth and nationality differ. Both specialists agree it is a false match. What must they do to close it?
options: Follow the internal procedure and keep a written justification for closure
Ask the customer to prove he is not the listed person
Close it verbally and move on
Freeze the account until SAMA confirms
bank.explanation: Rule 5.4 allows specialists to close a false match after the required procedure, keeping a written justification. Contacting the customer about the alert would breach confidentiality under 5.7.

bank.question: Wahat Bank's head of payments proposes using manual screening for a new remittance product to save costs. What do the TFS Rules say?
options: Manual screening is allowed if staff are trained
Manual tools need SAMA's written non-objection, and the exception does not apply to payment or transfer products
SAMA must be told after six months of use
Manual screening is always acceptable for small banks
bank.explanation: Rule 3.9 allows robust manual tools only with SAMA's written non-objection and conditions, and paragraph 3.9(f) excludes institutions offering payment or transfer products or services.

bank.question: A frozen account of a listed person receives an interest payment due under a contract signed before the freeze. What does TFS Rule 6.8 allow?
options: It may be paid out to the customer in cash
It must be returned to the payer
It must be paid to the FIU
The payment may be credited, but it stays frozen and SAMA is notified in writing
bank.explanation: Rule 6.8 allows payments, interest or earnings due under pre-freeze contracts, and certain inheritance or compensation funds, to be added, provided they remain frozen and SAMA is notified in writing.

bank.question: Which training element do the TFS Rules (8.3) require for the bank's sanctions unit?
options: Shadowing the FIU for one week
An annual e-learning module only
In-person workshops by specialist TFS trainers
A university degree in international law
bank.explanation: Rule 8.3 requires in-person workshops by trainers specialising in TFS for the relevant unit, while other units may use e-learning. Rule 8.2 adds simulation exercises for specialists.

bank.question: SAMA's December 2025 business risk guidance asks for one important distinction in the assessment. Which?
options: A clear distinction between ML, TF and proliferation financing risks
A distinction between paper and digital records
A distinction between Saudi and expatriate staff
A distinction between retail and corporate profits
bank.explanation: Paragraph 2.11(d) requires the business risk assessment to distinguish clearly between money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks.

bank.question: Wahat Bank wants to add repeated false matches to an internal whitelist so they stop generating alerts. Which condition applies under TFS Rule 5.8?
options: Deletion of the names after one year
Notification to the UN sanctions committee
Board or senior management approval, periodic review and continued screening of the list
Approval from the customer named on the list
bank.explanation: Rule 5.8 allows a justified internal whitelist only with board or senior management approval and periodic review, and the whitelist remains subject to comprehensive, post-update and event-based screening.

bank.question: Wahat Bank's risk team overrides an automated customer risk rating from high to medium. What does SAMA's December 2025 guidance (3.2.4) require?
options: SAMA's prior approval of every override
Automatic reversal after thirty days
No record, since overrides are a business decision
Governance of the override, with the decision and rationale documented
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3.2.4(e) requires governance of any decision to override an automated rating, with decisions and their rationale documented. Profitability must not drive ratings.

bank.question: Who must audit the business risk assessment, and how often, under SAMA's December 2025 guidance (2.6)?
options: The AML/CTF officer who prepared it, every two years
An independent auditor, at least once a year, reporting to the board or senior management
SAMA inspectors, every three years
The external auditor, only when the bank lists shares
bank.explanation: Paragraph 2.6 requires ongoing independent audit at least annually, covering methodology, data quality and control effectiveness, with results submitted to the board or senior management.

bank.question: The head of AML/CTF compliance at Wahat Bank also supervises the branch sales targets. Which SAMA principle is most at risk?
options: The independence of the AML/CTF compliance function
The ten-year record-keeping rule
The quarterly sanctions screening rule
The twelve-month transaction lookback
bank.explanation: Guide 9.1 requires the AML/CTF officer to work independently and report to the board and its committees. Combining the role with sales targets creates a conflict that undermines that independence.

bank.question: SAMA's Guide 12.6 asks banks to ensure employees take leave regularly and do not work during it. What is the AML/CTF purpose?
options: It improves the bank's customer satisfaction scores
It reduces the risk of staff hiding misconduct or circumventing controls
It is required to calculate end-of-service benefits
It allows the FIU to audit staff accounts
bank.explanation: Section 12 aims at staff integrity: background checks, possible job rotation and regular leave help expose collusion or concealment that depends on one person being always present.

bank.question: A director of Wahat Bank repeatedly ignored SAMA's AML findings. Which supervisory measure in Article 25 targets individuals directly?
options: Imprisonment for up to ten years
Deportation from the Kingdom
Banning individuals from working in sectors SAMA supervises
Confiscation of the director's personal property
bank.explanation: Article 25 lets SAMA ban individuals, restrict powers and dismiss or replace directors and executives. Prison, confiscation and deportation are criminal consequences imposed by courts, not supervisory measures.

bank.question: Under Article 31 of the AML Law, what fine can a court impose on a legal person convicted of money laundering?
options: Up to SAR 5 million per violation
Exactly the value of the funds involved
Up to SAR 7 million in aggravated cases
Up to SAR 50 million and not less than double the value of the funds involved
bank.explanation: Article 31 sets a fine of up to SAR 50 million and at least double the full value of the funds for legal persons. SAR 5 million per violation is SAMA's supervisory ceiling; SAR 7 million is the aggravated ceiling for individuals.

bank.question: In 2019 SAMA revoked Saeed Mohammed Ali Al-Amoudi & Co's licence to transfer funds. Which feature of that decision is most relevant for bank risk managers?
options: The decision was based only on capital shortfalls
SAMA fined the company SAR 50 million
SAMA removed one activity while allowing the company's other licensed activities to continue
The company's partners requested the revocation
bank.explanation: SAMA's announcement said it revoked the fund transfer licence and reclassified the company, while its other licensed activities continued, citing AML and CTF violations. It shows SAMA can target specific activities.

bank.question: SAMA's review finds Wahat Bank's training records show attendance but no knowledge tests for two years. Which requirement is most clearly unmet?
options: Keeping training records for ten years
Training new joiners before they start work
Allocating a training budget to senior management
Periodic testing of staff knowledge and training quality, at least annually
bank.explanation: Guide 11.4 requires knowledge and training-quality testing at least annually. Attendance records satisfy part of 11.5 but do not show that staff understood the material.
